description: After revocation the project disappears from `client list`, from `client status` and from the browser (which shows Welcome after a restart). The project folder under the data directory is named with an internal UUID rather than the project ID. Without a saved receipt the person cannot find the ID that `client export` needs.
expected: `client list --include-revoked` (or a `revoked[]` array) listing the name, ID and revocation time, and a revoked entry in the browser switcher with an Export action.
actual: No surface lists revoked project IDs.
suggested_fix: Keep revoked projects in the client list response under a separate key, and let `client export` accept a project name.

description: With the client stopped (so the connection file is stale), `client export` fails with `INTERNAL_ERROR: fetch failed`. The documented error is `CLIENT_NOT_RUNNING` "Start Pardner with pardner open or pardner client serve".
suggested_fix: Map connection-refused on the operator fetch to CLIENT_NOT_RUNNING in the shared CLI request helper (the same root cause as flag #25).

description: The "readable content export" is a 26 KB raw workspace document. It holds Actor hashes, revision IDs, the operation log and read receipts. Kevin wanted a private record of his task notes.
expected: A human-readable rendering (Markdown or HTML: tasks with status, description, comments and history) alongside the machine JSON.

description: `client export` silently overwrites an existing file at --output-file.
expected: Refuse when the file exists unless --force is passed, which matches the backup doc's `test ! -e` discipline.
actual: The file is overwritten without warning.
suggested_fix: Open the output with O_EXCL and return FILE_EXISTS.
